description:
**A submodule tasklist loses its story progress when a run restarts, even though its code survives.** Observed 2026-08-13 in insimul: `164-asset-libraries-and-suggestion` had reached **2/3** — US-1 and US-2 committed to `babylon/packages/core` as `feat:` commits — and after a run restart chief reported it at **0/3**.

**Root cause is the split.** For a submodule tasklist the TASKLIST lives in the parent (`insimul/tasks/chief/164-*.json`) while the WORK BRANCH lives in the submodule (`babylon/packages/core`). The parent has no `chief/*` branches at all, and every parent commit touching `tasks/chief/` is a terminal `complete @sha — bump <sub> + record + retire`. There is no per-story marker in between, so an interrupted submodule tasklist has nowhere to have recorded 2/3.

**The cost is re-verification, and the risk is worse than the cost.** An agent resuming at 0/3 checks out a branch where US-1 and US-2 code already exists. Best case it recognises the work and moves on, wasting iterations; worst case it **implements the story again**, leaving two implementations of one story on one branch — which is a genuinely messy state to unpick and exactly what the operator was warned to watch for.

This is not insimul-specific: it applies to any repo whose tasklists carry a `repo:` field pointing at a submodule, which is a first-class chief feature (`insimul/.chief/verify.sh` is explicitly *submodule-aware* and dispatches on it).

userStories.title: Per-story progress survives a restart for a submodule tasklist
userStories.description: Whatever the mechanism, the invariant is that resuming reports the progress the branch actually contains.
acceptanceCriteria: After a run is killed mid-tasklist and restarted, a submodule tasklist reports the SAME story count it had reached — asserted end-to-end against a fixture repo with a submodule, not by unit-testing the writer.

The mechanism is chosen and its trade-off recorded: a marker commit on the submodule branch, a parent-side branch, or state under `$STATE/`. Ephemeral state is acceptable ONLY if it survives a driver restart, which is the failure being fixed.

It does not change the terminal record: the parent still gets one `complete @sha — bump <sub> + record + retire` commit, so `completed/` history keeps its current shape and nothing downstream that reads it moves.
A NON-submodule tasklist's behaviour is byte-identical — asserted, since this is a fix to a special case and must not perturb the common one.
userStories.notes: test/submodule-resume.sh PASS — arm A: SIGKILLed the run's whole process group mid-turn, branch carried 2 story commits, durable snapshot banked 2, restart handed the agent 2/3 with US-3 next and worker logged "RESUMING chief/resume-demo (1 story left)"; arm C (non-submodule): identical kill/restart still resumed 2/3 at US-3 from the BRANCH's committed tasklist with the snapshot deliberately poisoned to 0. Counter-proof: with the promotion disabled on a temp commit the same test FAILS "no durable snapshot after the kill". Terminal record unmoved — exactly 2 commits touch tasks/chief (add + "resume-demo complete @sha — bump sub + record + retire"), completed/ record carries mergedToMain. Mechanism + rejected alternatives recorded in driver.sh prd_state_source. userStories.title: A resumed agent is told what is already done
userStories.description: Even with progress restored, an agent resuming onto a branch carrying prior work should be told so explicitly rather than inferring it from the diff.
acceptanceCriteria: On resume, the agent's context names which stories are already complete AND that their work is present on the checked-out branch — so 'already implemented' is a stated fact rather than something it must discover.

The guard against the worst case is explicit: the prompt states that re-implementing a completed story is a defect, since two implementations of one story on one branch is harder to unpick than an unfinished one.
Demonstrated on the real case: a fixture reproducing `insimul:164`'s shape (2 of 3 stories committed in a submodule, run restarted) resumes at story 3.
userStories.notes: test/submodule-resume.sh PASS — arm A now also asserts the PROMPT the resumed agent was handed (banked from the fake agent's stdin on its first turn): it carries the `# ALREADY DONE — work that is already committed on this branch` section, names `US-1 — one` and `US-2 — two`, does NOT list the unfinished `US-3 — three` among them, states `RE-IMPLEMENTING ONE OF THOSE STORIES IS A DEFECT`, and points at `Your work this turn is US-3`. Counterpart asserted too: the FIRST turn of the fresh (0-done) run carries no such section. Counter-proof — with the section gutted on a throwaway commit the same test FAILS "A: the resumed prompt never told the agent what is already done". Fixture is insimul:164's shape (2 of 3 committed in a submodule, SIGKILLed, restarted). Also green: bash -n clean over bin/ engine/ test/ (0 failures); version-bump PASS (0.8.61); doc-sync PASS; doc-links 4 dead vs 4 on main; quality ratchet OK (no metric regressed); behavioral — smoke, provider-conformance, ratelimit, limitstate, noworkguard, plan-review, research, liveliness, evidence-gate, measured-bars, boundary-demotion, criteria-scope, five-cases, stall-flag, headless, events, stale-resume, submodule-gitlink, submodule-resume all PASS (19).
